neighbours.label: the adverb after 'stir' in a recipe step (stir gently, stir occasionally, stir lightly), firing on the adverb; adverbs after other imperatives in the same frames stay low
fire: Add the rice to the pot and stir gently with a spoon.
Cook the lentils for twenty minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the cream, stir lightly and leave it to rest.
Stir frequently so that the onions do not burn.
Add the eggs one by one and stir thoroughly until smooth.
Let the jam bubble, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir briskly for one minute.
Lower the flame and stir occasionally until the sauce thickens.
quiet: Add the name to the list and sign neatly with a pen.
Walk the dogs for twenty minutes, stopping occasionally.
Pour in the gravel, rake lightly and leave it to settle.
Check frequently so that the children do not fall.
Add the boxes one by one and stack them carefully until full.
Let the horse run, riding slowly with a loose rein.
Open up the windows and sweep briskly for one minute.
Lower the blinds and read quietly until the storm passes.
